feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $G$ is a continuous vector field, then the flux of $G$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}G\cdot \,\text{d}S={∬}_{S}G\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that only the $z$-component of $G=⟨0,0,-xy-2{z}^{2}⟩$ is non-zero. Since the lateral sides of $S$ are parallel to the $z$-axis, the flux of $G$ through $S$ will be non-zero only at the top and bottom sides.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096328/assets/9e894018baf5f651e2d43cb48a324a5470c9061e6da10f666978519b3bff4c7f.png)

Let's consider the flux of $G$ through these two sides.

- Let ${S}_{1}$ denote the top surface. On this surface, we have $z=4$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector to ${S}_{1}$ is

$$
{n}_{1}=⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=4$ on ${S}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}G\cdot {n}_{1} & =⟨0,\,0,\,-xy-2{z}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-xy-32⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =-xy-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $G$ across ${S}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}G\cdot \text{d}{S}_{1} & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}G\cdot {n}_{1}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}(-xy-32)\,\text{d}S \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(xy+32)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(xy+32)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}y+32x]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}(2y+64)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{[{y}^{2}+64y]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =-132.\end{aligned}
$$

- Let ${S}_{2}$ denote the bottom surface. On this surface, we have $z=0$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector to ${S}_{2}$ is

$$
{n}_{2}=⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=0$ on ${S}_{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}G\cdot {n}_{2} & =⟨0,\,0,\,-xy-2{z}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-xy⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $G$ across ${S}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}G\cdot \text{d}{S}_{2} & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}G\cdot {n}_{2}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}xy\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =2\cdot 2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}G\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}G\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}G\cdot n\,\text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}G\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & =-132+4 \\  & =-128.\end{aligned}
$$
